title: Compliance Evidence & RBAC Operational Playbook
author: Aisha Mehta
content:
Overview
--------
This operational playbook consolidates RBAC & authorization guidance, audit logging expectations, data residency and retention requirements, secure SDLC checkpoints, incident-response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and the risk & exceptions process. It is intended for engineering leads, SREs, product owners, and security reviewers responsible for validating compliance during onboarding, audits, and deployments.

Scope and Purpose
------------------
- Scope: Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments; console and control-plane services; telemetry and audit pipelines.
- Purpose: Provide a single, actionable source of truth for operationalizing security controls and evidencing them to auditors (internal and external).

Ownership and Contacts
----------------------
- Process owner: Security (team lead: Aisha Mehta)
- Primary reviewers: Compliance (Sana Patel), Infra SRE (David Liu), Product Security (Evan Carter)
- Escalation path: security-oncall -> infra-oncall -> legal@redwood.com (for data-residency/legal holds)

Key Policies (summary)
----------------------
1) RBAC & Authorization
   - Principle: least privilege by default; roles = minimal functional sets.
   - Role categories: system-admin, infra-engineer, model-operator, tenant-admin (customer), observer, auditor.
   - Authentication: SSO (OIDC) via company IdP (Okta). MFA required for all interactive accounts; service-to-service auth uses short-lived mTLS certificates issued by internal CA.
   - Token lifetimes: interactive sessions 8 hours; API tokens 90 days (rotated programmatically).
   - Approval: any role granting of system-admin or tenant-admin requires manager + security approval and a JIRA ticket recorded.

2) Audit Logging
   - All access and control plane changes must emit auditable events to the audit-log cluster (Kafka -> immutable S3 bucket -> log-archival).
   - Minimum audit fields: timestamp, principal_id, principal_type (user/service), action, target_resource, request_id, source_ip, region, outcome (success/fail), change_delta (if applicable).
   - Retention: Audit logs replicated to cold storage for 7 years for enterprise customers with regulatory needs; standard retention is 3 years. See "Audit retention table" below.
   - Tamper-evidence: logs are hashed daily with an HMAC and the digest stored in KMS-protected metadata store.

3) Data Residency & Retention
   - Default: customer data at rest stored in the region selected at provisioning. Data movement across regions requires documented customer consent and security approval.
   - Backups: encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in-transit (TLS 1.3). Backup retention follows customer SLA; default 30 days for hosted customers.
   - Data deletion: documented deletion runbooks exist; deletion operations generate verifiable audit events and a deletion manifest for the customer.

4) Secure SDLC (development -> production)
   - Gating controls: PR must pass automated static analysis (SAST), dependency scanning (SCA), unit/integration tests, and security unit tests before merge.
   - Release process: artifacts signed (GPG) and provenance recorded in release metadata service (release-id).
   - Pre-deploy checks: infra-safe-config, secrets-scan, model-quantization-review (for model onboarding).

5) Incident Response - security procedures
   - Triage: Security oncall must be paged within 15 minutes of a suspected security incident.
   - Evidence preservation: snapshot affected host(s), preserve audit logs (write-once copy), and mark associated S3 prefixes with legal-hold flag.
   - Communication: use designated incident bridge; customer-facing comms coordinated by Security + CS + Legal.

Operational Procedures (step-by-step)
-------------------------------------
A. Compliance Evidence Collection (for audits)
   1. Create an Evidence Request ticket (label: evidence-request) in JIRA with scope and time window.
   2. Security will map evidence templates to requested controls (ISO/ SOC/ GDPR). Templates available at /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/templates.
   3. Run the evidence collection job (infra tool):
      - CLI: ./tools/evidence-collector collect --scope "control:RBAC" --since 2024-01-01 --to 2024-12-31 --out /tmp/evidence.zip
      - Output: zipped artifacts: audit-log-extract.jsonl, role-matrix.csv, config-dump.yaml, SSO-assertions.txt
   4. Security reviews artifacts, annotates controls, and uploads to compliance evidence store (internal S3) with access restricted to auditors and security.
   5. Provide auditor read-only IAM role for the evidence bucket; generate time-limited access links (max 7 days).

B. Role Granting & RBAC Change Workflow
   1. Initiate ticket in Access Requests board with requested role, reason, duration.
   2. Auto-check: ticket included manager approval and least-privilege justification.
   3. Security reviews if role = system-admin or privileges cross multiple services.
   4. Apply change using access-ctl tool with audit trail:
      - access-ctl grant --principal alice@redwood.com --role infra-engineer --expires 2025-05-01 --ticket RED-1234
   5. Post-change review: owner-team has 48 hours to confirm the change; if not confirmed, flag for auto-revoke 7 days later.

C. Data Residency Exception / Risk & Exceptions Process
   1. If a workload requires cross-region replication against default policy, submit an Exception Request (ER) with: business justification, data classification, technical mitigation, duration, and compensating controls.
   2. Security evaluates ER; high-risk ERs require CISO + Legal signoff.
   3. Approved ERs generate a documented mitigation plan and ticket that includes required monitoring (e.g., enhanced audit sampling, weekly infra reports).

Tables & Thresholds (described as text tables)
------------------------------------------------
- Audit retention table:
  - Standard customers: 3 years
  - Regulated customers (signed contract): 7 years
  - Critical infra events (auth failures, admin role assignments): 10 years in immutable storage

- SLOs & Alerting thresholds:
  - Audit pipeline ingestion latency: 99th percentile < 15s (alert at 30s sustained for 5m)
  - Evidence collection job success rate: > 99% per week (alert < 95%)
  - RBAC drift (users with unexpected privilege): < 0.5% of active users (alert at 1%)

Roles & Permissions matrix (abridged)
-------------------------------------
- system-admin: create/delete resources, grant roles, view all audit logs (requires 2FA + approval).
- infra-engineer: deploy infra resources, read-most logs, not allowed to grant tenant-admin.
- model-operator: deploy model assets, trigger canary rollouts, no access to customer PII.
- tenant-admin: customer-managed role, isolated to their tenant region.
- auditor: read-only access to audit logs and evidence store.

Audit log example (JSON-line)
----------------------------
{"timestamp":"2025-02-01T14:03:21Z","principal_id":"alice@redwood.com","principal_type":"user","action":"role.grant","target_resource":"service/api-gateway","request_id":"req-9a7f","source_ip":"34.200.11.23","region":"us-west-2","outcome":"success","change_delta":"{\"role\":\"infra-engineer\"}"}

Security Controls - Implementation notes
----------------------------------------
- SSO / OIDC: Okta config: session.maxAge=8h, requireMFA=true. Keep provisioning via SCIM.
- Service auth: envoy-based mTLS; cert rotation via cert-manager, 90-day rotation cycle.
- Audit pipeline: kafka-topic: audit-events, consumer group: audit-collector, writer: s3-audit-writer. Use IAM role with kms:Encrypt and kms:Decrypt disabled for auditor-role (read-only).
- Secrets management: all secrets in Vault; RBAC bound to Kubernetes service accounts using sigstore for release verification.

Checklist for quarterly compliance readiness
-------------------------------------------
- [ ] Evidence collection run for past quarter completed and archived.
- [ ] RBAC review: remove stale roles and accounts > 90 days inactive.
- [ ] Audit pipeline health OK (ingestion latency & consumer lag checks).
- [ ] Secure SDLC gating passing on all active repos.
- [ ] Incident-response tabletop executed within past 6 months.

Appendix: Common Commands & Examples
-----------------------------------
- Evidence collector (example):
  ./tools/evidence-collector collect --controls RBAC,AUDIT --since 2024-10-01 --out evidence_q4_2024.zip

- Grant role (example):
  access-ctl grant --principal bob@customer.com --role tenant-admin --scope tenant-123 --ticket RED-2048

- Revoke inactive accounts (dry run):
  ./scripts/rbac-audit --dry-run --inactive-days 90 --out stale_accounts.csv
